title: Tensor compatibility of transported Picard pullback composition
statement: Let X,Y,Z be schemes [def-pc-scheme], k:Z→Y and l:Y→X, and M,N O_X-modules. Use tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], the comparison δ [def-sc-picard-cup-product-map], and the fixed composition comparison c [lem-sc-picard-canonical-base-change-comparisons]. Then δ_k inverse followed by P_k(δ_l inverse) and c_(M tensor N) equals (c_M tensor c_N) followed by δ_(k followed by l) inverse, exactly as lean.statement. No pairing or unit map occurs.

source.place: Definition 6.26.1(2), tensor formula; Tag 0096, adjunction normalizing the composition comparison. Expanded tensor/unit-composition argument of lem-sc-picard-pairing-composition.

proof.text: Expand the comparison definitions, combine functor maps and tensor morphisms, and cancel the adjacent comparison inverses and homs. Use naturality of picardTensorComparison k and of the ordinary tensorator to move the argument comparisons before the ordinary tensorators.
Apply ordinary pullbackComp_tensor to the two ordinary tensorators followed by composition. Tensor functoriality and associativity identify the result with the expanded right side.

lean.statement:
theorem picardTensorObjIso_comp_inv
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (k : Z ⟶ Y) (l : Y ⟶ X) (M N : X.Modules) :
    (picardTensorObjIso k ((tensorPullback l).obj M) ((tensorPullback l).obj N)).inv ≫
      (tensorPullback k).map (picardTensorObjIso l M N).inv ≫
        (picardTensorCompIso k l (M ⊗ N)).hom =
    ((picardTensorCompIso k l M).hom ⊗ₘ (picardTensorCompIso k l N).hom) ≫
      (picardTensorObjIso (k ≫ l) M N).inv
